subject: Deployment mode evaluation checklist + MAP — EU data residency and close runway
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medisys.com>, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@medisys.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode evaluation checklist + MAP — EU data residency and close runway

Carlos / Emma,

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, I wanted to put a short mutual action plan (MAP) and an evaluation checklist on the table so we can lock the deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and the region gating. The core asks we heard are: EU data residency, predictable latency for inference, and a procurement timeline that lands by mid-March.

I've attached a one-page MAP draft and a quick SLA comparison to help. High level proposal:
- Week 1: Confirm residency + legal pre-reqs (KMS, DPA scope)
- Week 2-3: PoC (40k tokens/day synthetic load) on a hosted EU region variant + parallel Dedicated perf run if you want throughput guarantees
- Week 4: Quality & regression signoff, procurement SOW, finalize deployment mode

Decision criteria we'll use in the MAP: data residency (must be EU), latency P95 < 200ms for 512 token sequences, per-token cost target for 95% of trajectories, and support/SLAs. If Private is required for regulatory reasons we'll add a private VPC path and update timelines (likely +3 weeks).

Could you confirm: (1) EU-only data residency requirement is absolute, and (2) whether your procurement team needs an early SOW draft this week?

I'll loop in Steph and Dylan on the next message for technical constraints and lead times.

Best,
Ben
--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0112

Attachments: RINF-MAP-draft-v1.pdf (MAP draft), SLA-comparison-brief.xlsx (summary)

From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medisys.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode evaluation checklist + MAP — EU data residency and close runway

Hi Ben,

Thanks — that looks useful. Quick answers up front: EU-only residency is non-negotiable (we're bound by our DPA and a pending audit).

We prefer Dedicated if it gets us predictable throughput and helps meet our latency goals, but we need to understand lead-time and cost delta vs Hosted. Private (VPC) is on the table only if legal requires it after we review the SOW.

Our procurement team would like an SOW draft this week to start internal approvals — can you provide a short SOW and SOC2 evidence links? Also, can we run a short Dedicated perf run in parallel with the Hosted PoC? We want apples-to-apples latency/cost numbers.

Best,
Carlos Ruiz
SVP Prod Ops | MediSys Health
c.ruiz@medisys.com

Carlos — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Looping Steph (legal/enterprise) and Dylan (solutions) to confirm practical lead times and to propose an exact runbook.

Dylan / Steph — summary: MediSys requires EU-only residency; they prefer Dedicated for predictability but want a Hosted baseline. They asked for:
- SOW draft this week
- SOC2 evidence
- Parallel Dedicated perf run + Hosted PoC for apples-to-apples comparison

Draft runbook proposal (short):
1) Today-T+3: Share SOW draft + SOC2 evidence bundle (we can provide redacted SOC2 artifacts and SOC2 attestation PDF)
2) T+3 to T+10: Hosted EU PoC (single-node in eu-west) — 3 business days runtime with fixed synthetic load (we'll provide script)
3) T+5 to T+12: Dedicated perf run (reserved capacity in eu-west) — note: provisioning Dedicated capacity lead time is currently 10 business days unless we allocate warm-capacity from our pool
4) T+12 to T+17: QA/regression checks and signoff; procurement completes SOW

Key constraints to call out:
- If they choose Private, we need an on-prem/VPC kickstart window and that adds ~3 weeks depending on network onboarding and certs.
- Dedicated provisioning can be accelerated if we apply a one-time implementation fee to use pre-warmed nodes (we should confirm pricing/discount).

I attached the initial MAP and SLA brief. I'll iterate the MAP based on your input.

Ben

Ben / Dylan — quick internal notes before we send the SOW:
- Procurement: MediSys will likely request a 60-day invoice payment term and a one-time discount tied to a 12-month committed Dedicated plan. We should flag discount approval thresholds (VP Sales signoff for >15%).
- Security: We can share the SOC2 attestation and a redacted control matrix this week. For Private/VPC, we need to book an infra onboarding slot — typically 8-12 working days for network and KMS integration windows.
- Ops: If we promise Dedicated perf within two weeks, we should plan to use warm-capacity; confirm uplift fee with finance.

I'll prepare a clean SOW template with two variants (Hosted baseline + Dedicated committed) and a short Private appendix in case legal flips. Ben — want me to send the SOW to Carlos directly or should you?

Appended a slightly updated MAP (v2) and a short SOW sketch (Hosted + Dedicated options). Key changes:
- Explicit EU residency clause included in SOW sketch
- Dedicated warm-capacity option called out (+1.2x implementation fee) to accelerate provisioning to within 3 business days
- Acceptance criteria: latency P95 <200ms (512 tokens) for Hosted run; Dedicated should improve P95 by >=15% on average under target load

- Sign SOW by 2026-02-18
- PoC comparison runs complete by 2026-03-05
- Procurement + SOW finalization by 2026-03-12
- Go-live (initial tranche) 2026-03-22

Next steps I propose: you confirm whether we should accelerate Dedicated provisioning (we can offer the warm-capacity path if procurement agrees to the uplift), and if you want the SOW and SOC2 bundle in DocuSign or as a PDF to start legal review.

Thanks — I'll keep the MAP live and update as we agree.

Best,
Ben
